Motor neuronopathy is primary. Structural muscle wasting in 7/8 supports musculoskeletal involvement. Left ventricular hypertrophy in 2/6 meets the approximate 30% threshold; medium confidence reflects the limited sample.

Purine metabolism dysfunction and defining neurodevelopmental abnormalities support the primary axes. Renal insufficiency and sensorineural hearing impairment each occur in 30-79%; separately diagnosed gout and stones do not add axes.

Myocardial dilatation, fibrosis, impaired ventricular function and conduction disease establish cardiovascular disease. Antibody positivity, vertigo and dyspnea do not establish additional organ damage.
